docs.title: About Me
docs.text:
I am a Water Resources Engineer and Researcher working at the intersection of hydrology and machine learning. My work focuses on applying data-driven methods to environmental and hydrological challenges — from sensitivity analysis of hydrological models to predicting water quality in urban waterways.

I hold an M.Sc. in Water Resources Engineering and Management from Sharif University of Technology and a B.Sc. in Civil Engineering from the University of Tehran. I am currently applying to Ph.D. programs to continue developing hybrid physics–machine learning frameworks for environmental systems.

Research vision. My M.Sc. thesis compared machine learning surrogates against classical variance-based methods for sensitivity analysis of hydrological models, and my current work as a Graduate Research Assistant applies ensemble learning to real-time odor pollution prediction in urban canals. Across both, my interest lies in the same open question: how can data-driven models be made trustworthy enough — physically consistent, uncertainty-aware, and interpretable — to support real decisions about water infrastructure. In a Ph.D., I want to push this further by developing hybrid physics–ML frameworks that couple process-based hydrological models with modern deep learning, with a focus on rigorous sensitivity and uncertainty quantification for environmental and climate-resilience applications.

docs.title: Evaluating Machine Learning Methods for Variance-based Sensitivity Analysis in Hydrological Models
docs.text:
Global sensitivity analysis (GSA) is essential for understanding which parameters govern hydrological model behavior, but classical variance-based estimators (e.g., Sobol indices) become computationally expensive at scale. This thesis benchmarked a machine-learning surrogate — Random Forest Permutation Variable Importance (RF-PVI) — against the Sobol total-order index across convergence, robustness, accuracy, and computational cost, using the HBV hydrological model on the Bow River Basin as a case study.

Graphical abstract — Monte Carlo sampling, HBV model runs, RF-PVI computation, and Sobol total-order estimation, evaluated against convergence, robustness, accuracy, and computational time. HBVSobol IndicesRandom ForestMonte CarloPython
